sources.title: Request production access (Moving out of the Amazon SES sandbox)
supports: New accounts start in the SES sandbox, and the sandbox status is per Region
In the sandbox: mail only to verified addresses and domains or the mailbox simulator, at most 200 messages per 24 hours, at most 1 message per second
In the sandbox, bulk actions and SES API calls for suppression list management are disabled
After leaving the sandbox, From, Source, Sender and Return-Path identities still have to be verified
The console request asks for mail type (Marketing or Transactional), website URL, up to 4 additional contact addresses, preferred contact language (English or Japanese), and an acknowledgement
`aws sesv2 put-account-details --production-access-enabled --mail-type --website-url --additional-contact-email-addresses --contact-language` submits the same request
AWS Support gives an initial response within 24 hours; details cannot be edited while the review is open

sources.title: Using the Amazon SES account-level suppression list
supports: The account-level suppression list applies to one account in one Region
Accounts that started using SES after 2019-11-25 use it by default for bounces and complaints
A message to a suppressed address (with a matching reason) is accepted by SES but not sent
Such messages count toward the daily sending quota, and not toward the reputation bounce and complaint rates
Only hard bounces are added; addresses stay until removed
Gmail does not provide complaint data to SES
PutSuppressedDestination and CreateImportJob are unavailable in the sandbox
A configuration set can override the account-level suppression settings; with it, addresses are added only for mail sent with that configuration set
List entries are case-sensitive in the management API
`aws sesv2 put-account-suppression-attributes`, `list-suppressed-destinations`, and `delete-suppressed-destination`

sources.title: How email sending works in Amazon SES
supports: A successful request returns a message ID; delivery, bounce, and complaint happen afterwards
On rare occasions SES may accept an email for delivery even though the send request returns an error; a retry may then send a second email with a different message ID
SES recommends message tags, not only the message ID, to correlate event notifications with sending logic
Definitions of hard bounce and soft bounce; SES retries soft bounces for a period before reporting them

sources.title: SES API v2: SendEmail
supports: Request fields used: FromEmailAddress, Destination.ToAddresses, Content.Simple, ConfigurationSetName, EmailTags
The request has no idempotency or client token parameter
The response is a MessageId, and SES can accept a message without sending it

Errors: AccountSuspendedException, BadRequestException, LimitExceededException, MailFromDomainNotVerifiedException, MessageRejected, SendingPausedException (400), NotFoundException (404), TooManyRequestsException (429)

sources.title: SES API v2: MessageTag
supports: Tag names and values: ASCII letters, digits, underscore and dash only, at most 256 characters

sources.title: Monitor email sending using Amazon SES event publishing
supports: Events are published only for mail sent with a configuration set that has an event destination
Meaning of the Send, Delivery, Bounce, Complaint, Reject and DeliveryDelay events
Delivery means delivered to the recipient's mail server
Message tags and auto-tags are included in published events

sources.title: Contents of event data that Amazon SES publishes to Amazon SNS
supports: Top-level fields eventType, mail, bounce, complaint, delivery, and the possible eventType values
mail.messageId and mail.tags; bounce.bounceType, bounceSubType, bouncedRecipients[].emailAddress, timestamp, feedbackId
bounceType is Undetermined, Permanent or Transient; Permanent includes the OnAccountSuppressionList subtype
Only hard bounces, and soft bounces SES has stopped retrying, are published
Most ISPs redact the complainer's address, so complainedRecipients lists every recipient of the mail on the complaining domain

sources.title: Examples of event data that Amazon SES publishes to Amazon SNS
supports: The Bounce, Complaint and Delivery example records that examples/15-email/test/fixtures/ follow
sources.note: The fixtures are edited copies of the documented examples. No event was captured from a real account.

sources.title: Set up an Amazon SNS event destination for event publishing
supports: SES supports standard SNS topics only as an event destination, not FIFO
The topic policy must allow sns:Publish to ses.amazonaws.com, conditioned on AWS:SourceAccount and the configuration set's AWS:SourceArn

sources.title: Creating and verifying identities in Amazon SES
supports: An identity is a domain or an email address, verified separately in each Region
Verifying a domain covers its addresses and subdomains
An address verified only through its domain is limited to straightforward sending; advanced sending includes using the address with configuration sets
Email address identities are case-sensitive; the verification mail comes from no-reply-aws@amazon.com and its link expires after 24 hours
A domain identity is verified by publishing three Easy DKIM CNAME records, which can take up to 72 hours to be detected
The CNAME value is the token followed by the SigningHostedZone returned by CreateEmailIdentity and GetEmailIdentity
sources.note: What "using the address with configuration sets" excludes for an address that is verified only through its domain is not spelled out. The stack sets the configuration set as the identity's default as well as naming it on each send.

sources.title: Easy DKIM in Amazon SES
supports: With Easy DKIM, SES signs every mail from the identity with a 2048-bit key by default
The SES console can publish the records itself when Route 53 hosts the domain

sources.title: Using a custom MAIL FROM domain
supports: By default the MAIL FROM domain is a subdomain of amazonses.com, and SPF passes for that domain
A custom MAIL FROM domain must be a subdomain of the verified identity's domain, not used for sending or receiving
It needs exactly one MX record `10 feedback-smtp.<region>.amazonses.com` and a TXT record "v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all"
Behavior on MX failure is either falling back to the default MAIL FROM domain or rejecting the message
SES looks for the MX record for up to 72 hours

sources.title: Complying with DMARC authentication protocol in Amazon SES
supports: SPF checks the MAIL FROM domain, DKIM checks the signing domain, and DMARC requires one of them to align with the From domain
A message passes DMARC if either the SPF or the DKIM alignment check passes
The DMARC policy is a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain>; p=none, quarantine, and reject, rolled out in that order
SPF alignment through SES needs a custom MAIL FROM domain; DKIM alignment needs Easy DKIM on the From domain
`dig TXT _dmarc.<domain>` shows the published policy

sources.title: Sending test emails in Amazon SES with the simulator
supports: success@, bounce@, complaint@, ooto@ and suppressionlist@simulator.amazonses.com and what each simulates
The simulator works in the sandbox
Simulator mail does not count toward the daily quota or the bounce and complaint rates, and is billed like any other mail
bounce@simulator.amazonses.com is not placed on the suppression list

sources.title: SES API v2: GetAccount
supports: ProductionAccessEnabled false means the account is in the sandbox in that Region
SendQuota (Max24HourSend, MaxSendRate, SentLast24Hours), SendingEnabled, EnforcementStatus, SuppressionAttributes.SuppressedReasons

sources.title: SES API v2: GetEmailIdentity
supports: VerifiedForSendingStatus, VerificationStatus (PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, TEMPORARY_FAILURE, NOT_STARTED)
DkimAttributes (Status, Tokens, SigningHostedZone) and MailFromAttributes (MailFromDomain, MailFromDomainStatus)
Without an event destination or another mechanism, bounce and complaint notifications are sent by email

sources.title: AWS Service Reference: actions, resources and condition keys for SES
supports: ses:SendEmail is authorized against the resource types identity, configuration-set and template
ARN formats arn:aws:ses:<region>:<account>:identity/<name> and :configuration-set/<name>
ses:SendEmail supports the condition keys ses:FromAddress, ses:FromDisplayName, ses:Recipients, ses:FeedbackAddress and ses:ApiVersion
sources.note: The JSON does not mark which resource types are required. Whether a sandbox account also needs permission on the recipient's identity was not confirmed from a primary source.

sources.title: Amazon SES pricing
supports: Outbound email is USD 0.10 per 1,000 emails, charged per recipient, plus USD 0.12 per GB of attachments
The page describes Free Tier credits for new AWS customers (up to USD 200, a free plan available for 6 months, credits to be used within 12 months) and no monthly count of free messages
Dedicated IPs and Virtual Deliverability Manager are separate charges
sources.note: Read as rendered on 2026-10-11. The Free Tier terms depend on when and how an account was created; the calculation applies no allowance.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: SES, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonSES
Mail to the mailbox simulator has its own SKU at the same USD 0.0001 per recipient

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: SNS, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonSNS
The first 1,000,000 SNS API requests a month are a USD 0 tier
Deliveries to Lambda are USD 0

sources.title: Invoking Lambda functions with Amazon SNS notifications
supports: SNS invokes the function asynchronously; only standard topics are supported
Asynchronous invocations process each event at least once, and duplicates can occur
The event shape: Records[].Sns.Message and MessageId

sources.title: How Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation
supports: When the function returns an error, Lambda runs it two more times by default
A function can receive the same event more than once even without an error
An event that fails all attempts is discarded unless a dead-letter queue or an on-failure destination is configured

sources.title: Amazon SNS message delivery retries
supports: When SNS cannot reach a Lambda endpoint it makes up to 100,015 attempts over 23 days
When the delivery policy is exhausted the message is discarded unless the subscription has a dead-letter queue

sources.title: AWS SDKs and Tools: Retry behavior
supports: The default is 3 attempts in total; max attempts 1 disables retries
Timeouts, connection failures and HTTP 500, 502, 503, 504 are retried as transient errors; TooManyRequestsException as throttling

sources.title: Control access to HTTP APIs with IAM authorization in API Gateway
supports: With IAM authorization on a route, clients sign requests with SigV4, and API Gateway invokes the route only if the caller has execute-api permission
Resource policies are not supported for HTTP APIs

sources.title: Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB
supports: The TTL attribute is a Number holding Unix epoch seconds
Expired items are deleted typically within a few days of expiring, without consuming write throughput
Until then an expired item can still be read and updated

sources.title: Email settings for Amazon Cognito user pools
supports: The default email configuration limits the number of emails per day and is below typical production volume
With the SES configuration, the user pool sends through a verified identity in your account, under your SES limits
The account must be out of the SES sandbox before Cognito can mail users through your SES configuration
sources.note: The daily limit of the default configuration is on the Cognito quotas page, which was not read.

sources.title: Cloudflare Email Service
supports: Email Sending is in beta for outbound transactional email
A Worker sends through a send_email binding (env.EMAIL.send); a REST API and SMTP also exist
Email Sending requires the Workers Paid plan
sources.note: Only the overview page was read. Domain onboarding, DNS records, bounce handling, limits and prices were not checked.

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28: provider routing for the resource types of chapter 15 (npm tarball)
supports: No SDK provider is registered for AWS::SES::EmailIdentity, AWS::SES::ConfigurationSet or AWS::SES::ConfigurationSetEventDestination; types without one are routed to Cloud Control API

AWS::SNS::Topic, AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy, AWS::SNS::Subscription, AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Permission, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy and the four AWS::ApiGatewayV2 types have registered SDK providers
sources.note: Read from dist/ of the published tarball (the bundled register calls and the provider registry). No cdkd command was run against AWS, so the Cloud Control path for the SES types is unexercised.

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-ses constructs (type definitions and compiled source)
supports: EmailIdentity exposes dkimRecords, and accepts configurationSet, mailFromDomain and mailFromBehaviorOnMxFailure
ConfigurationSet.addEventDestination with an SNS topic also adds a topic policy for ses.amazonaws.com conditioned on the configuration set's ARN
ConfigurationSet.suppressionReasons synthesizes SuppressionOptions.SuppressedReasons

definition.ja: SES に「自分のものだ」と確認してもらった送信元。ドメインか、メールアドレス 1 つ。リージョンごとに確認する。
definition.en: A sender that SES has verified as yours: a domain or a single email address. Verified per Region.

definition.ja: 新しいアカウントの SES が置かれる制限つきの状態。確認済みの宛先にしか送れない。production access を申請して出る。
definition.en: The restricted state every new account's SES starts in: mail goes only to verified recipients. Left by requesting production access.

definition.ja: メールが届かずに戻ってくること。宛先が存在しないなどの恒久的なもの（hard）と、一時的なもの（soft）がある。
definition.en: Mail that comes back undelivered. Permanent (hard), such as an address that does not exist, or temporary (soft).

definition.ja: 受信者がメールを「迷惑メール」と報告すること。
definition.en: A recipient reporting a mail as spam.

definition.ja: もう送らないと決めた宛先の一覧。bounce や complaint を出した宛先を入れる。
definition.en: The list of addresses you will no longer mail, filled with those that bounced or complained.

definition.ja: SES で、送信時に指定する設定のまとまり。イベントの配送先や suppression の設定を持つ。
definition.en: A named group of SES settings chosen at send time, holding event destinations and suppression options.

definition.ja: 「このドメインの名前で送ってよいサーバー」を DNS の TXT レコードで公開する仕組み。見るのは封筒の差出人（MAIL FROM）のドメイン。
definition.en: A DNS TXT record naming the servers allowed to send for a domain. It is checked against the envelope sender (MAIL FROM) domain.

definition.ja: メールに電子署名を付け、検証用の公開鍵を DNS で公開する仕組み。
definition.en: A digital signature on each mail, verified with a public key published in DNS.

definition.ja: 受信者に見える From のドメインが、SPF か DKIM のどちらかで確かめられていることを求め、失敗したメールの扱いを DNS で指示する仕組み。
definition.en: A DNS policy that requires the visible From domain to be confirmed by SPF or DKIM, and says what to do with mail that fails.

tiers.description: USD0.0001 per Count for Recipients:Send in Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
First 1,000,000 Amazon SNS API Requests per month are free
$0.50 per 1,000,000 Amazon SNS API Requests per month thereafter
There is no charge for Lambda Notifications

unknownAllowances.reason: The SES pricing page describes Free Tier credits for new customers, whose terms depend on the account, and no monthly count of free messages. None is applied.

title.ja: 通知メール: デプロイ済みで 1 通も送らない月
title.en: Notification mail: deployed, but nothing sent for a month

ja: 送信ゼロ、イベントゼロ
table に 10 MB の記録（送信停止の一覧と、期限前の通知の記録）
en: 10 MB of records in the table (suppressions and unexpired notification records)

title.ja: 通知メール: 月 1 万通

ja: 通知 1 件につき宛先 1 つ、添付なし。月 10,000 通
同じ通知の重複依頼が 1,000 件（送信はしないが、API と関数は動く）
1 通につき SES のイベントが 1 件（delivery、bounce、complaint のどれか）届く
送信の関数は平均 300 ミリ秒、イベントの関数は平均 50 ミリ秒。どちらも 256 MB、arm64
DynamoDB の書き込みは 1 通あたり 3 回（先取り、送信済み、イベント）、重複依頼は 1 回。読み取りは依頼 1 件につき結果整合で 1 回、重複依頼ではさらに強い整合性で 1 回
ログは依頼とイベントを合わせて 1 件あたり 0.5 KB
インターネットへのデータ転送、専用 IP、Virtual Deliverability Manager は未算入
en: One recipient per notification, no attachments; 10,000 messages a month
1,000 repeated requests for a notification already handled (nothing is sent, but the API and the function run)
One SES event per message (a delivery, a bounce or a complaint)
The sending function averages 300 ms and the event function 50 ms, both at 256 MB on arm64
Three DynamoDB writes per message (claim, sent, event) and one per repeated request; one eventually consistent read per request, plus one strongly consistent read per repeated request
0.5 KB of logs per request and per event
Data transfer out, dedicated IPs and Virtual Deliverability Manager are not included

items.basis: one delivery to the function per event
11,000 suppression checks x 0.5 + 1,000 consistent reads of an existing record x 1

note.ja: ヘッダー injection の拒否、記録を先に取る送信の冪等性（8 か所の障害注入、同時依頼、応答喪失）、SES イベントの検証と重複・順序の入れ替わり、DynamoDB と SES へ送るリクエストの検査、インフラの assertion
note.en: Header-injection refusals, record-first idempotent sending (faults injected at eight points, simultaneous requests, lost responses), validation of SES events with duplicates and reordering, inspection of the requests sent to DynamoDB and SES, and infrastructure assertions

summary.ja: 15章は SES を一度も呼んでいない。identity の確認、送信 role の policy（ses:FromAddress の条件、identity と configuration set の 2 つの resource）で SendEmail が通ること、sandbox で宛先の identity にも権限が要るかどうか、実際のイベントが fixture と同じ形であること、SNS から関数への配送、configuration set の suppression の動きは未確認。
summary.en: Chapter 15 never called SES. Unconfirmed: identity verification, SendEmail passing under the sending role's policy (the ses:FromAddress condition and the two resources, identity and configuration set), whether a sandbox account also needs permission on the recipient's identity, real events matching the fixtures, delivery from SNS to the function, and the configuration set's suppression behavior.

resume.ja: 自分のアドレスで vp run mail:infra:deploy -c fromAddress=... を実行して確認メールのリンクを踏み、vp run mail:send --to 自分のアドレス、続けて --to bounce@simulator.amazonses.com と complaint@simulator.amazonses.com を実行する。mail:status と mail:logs --events で状態とイベントを確かめ、届いたイベントの JSON を test/fixtures と比べる。AccessDenied が出たら、エラーに出た resource の ARN を記録する。
resume.en: Run vp run mail:infra:deploy -c fromAddress=... with your own address, follow the link in the verification mail, then run vp run mail:send --to your address, and again with --to bounce@simulator.amazonses.com and complaint@simulator.amazonses.com. Check the states and events with mail:status and mail:logs --events, and compare the received event JSON with test/fixtures. If AccessDenied appears, record the resource ARN the error names.

summary.ja: cdkd 0.296.28 は AWS::SES::EmailIdentity、ConfigurationSet、ConfigurationSetEventDestination に専用の実装を持たず、Cloud Control API 経由になる。この経路での作成、更新、drift の検出、削除は一度も動かしていない。DKIM の token を output として読めるかも未確認。
summary.en: cdkd 0.296.28 has no dedicated provider for AWS::SES::EmailIdentity, ConfigurationSet or ConfigurationSetEventDestination, so they go through Cloud Control API. Create, update, drift detection and delete on that path were never run, and reading the DKIM tokens as outputs is unconfirmed.

resume.ja: vp run mail:infra:deploy、mail:infra:drift、mail:infra:destroy を実行する。ドメインの identity では vp run mail:dns が DkimName1〜3 と DkimValue1〜3 を読めることを確かめる。
resume.en: Run vp run mail:infra:deploy, mail:infra:drift and mail:infra:destroy. With a domain identity, confirm that vp run mail:dns can read DkimName1-3 and DkimValue1-3.

summary.ja: 15章の「同じ通知は 1 通」は、条件付きの PutItem が同時の依頼を 1 つだけ通すことに依存する。確かめたのは、送っている条件式と、メモリの実装が同じ規則に従うことだけで、DynamoDB Local でも実際の DynamoDB でも動かしていない。
summary.en: Chapter 15's "one notification, one mail" depends on a conditional PutItem letting exactly one of several simultaneous requests through. Only the expression sent, and the in-memory implementation's adherence to the same rule, were checked; neither DynamoDB Local nor real DynamoDB was used.

resume.ja: デプロイ後、同じ notificationId の依頼を並行で送る script を examples/15-email/scripts/ に加え、届いたメールが 1 通であることを受信箱と mail:status で確かめる。
resume.en: After deploying, add a script under examples/15-email/scripts/ that sends requests with one notificationId in parallel, and confirm in the inbox and with mail:status that one mail arrived.
